newsitem.title: UK: Lockheed faces UK fines of 20-40 mln stg.
newsitem.headline: Lockheed faces UK fines of 20-40 mln stg.

text.p: Lockheed Martin Corp, the U.S. aerospace giant, faces fines of between 20 and 40 million pounds ($32.5 to $64.9 million) owing to the late delivery of new transport aircraft to Britain's Royal Air Force (RAF), the Financial Times said on Tuesday.

The newspaper said the delay would be an embarrassment for Lockheed, which won the one billion pound contract to supply 25 new Hercules C-130J aircraft in 1994 after a bitter battle against the alternative European Future Large Aircraft.
Development problems meant the contracted delivery date of November 1996 was not met and the first aircraft would not now be delivered until late this year at the earliest.

The delays have meant that the RAF has had to continue flying its old C-130H aircraft which are increasingly expensive to maintain. Lockheed has to reimburse the UK Ministry of Defence for the extra costs, which range between 20 and 40 million pounds depending on how quickly the company can make up the lost time. ($ = 0.616 British Pounds)
